sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy), RCS District of Luxembourg
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (mixed French and German legal tradition with EU-harmonized corporate and AML/CFT statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America (signed 3 April 1996, amended by Protocol of 20 May 2009)
Double Taxation Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Federal Republic of Germany
Double Taxation Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China
Annex XII to the EU Single Market: free movement of goods and services (relevant to EU-wide e-commerce retail)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU)-China investment protection agreements (BIT line)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 904-1 to 904-13 (Special Limited Partnership – SCSp – provisions as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement / Contrat de Société (Articles of Association of the SCSp) filed electronically via the LBR online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp. Capital contributions are freely determined by the partnership agreement. Monetary contributions must be credited to a Luxembourg bank account held in the name of the SCSp, and all contribution records must be maintained by the general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by AB, the sole general partner of the SCSp, acting by written consent: (i) the registered office of the Partnership shall be fixed at [address], Luxembourg; (ii) the formation documents, including the partnership agreement and the management declaration, are approved in final form; (iii) the capital subscription records are approved, confirming that no statutory minimum capital applies and that all contributions shall be credited in accordance with the agreement; (iv) CD is appointed manager of the Partnership with full authority to open bank accounts and file registrations; and (v) the general partner is authorized to cause the filing of the formation dossier with the Luxembourg Business Registers and the publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Registered Office Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online portal, and the landlord/domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search on the LBR portal and reserve the proposed corporate name of the SCSp if permitted. Obtain a signed written consent from the landlord or licensed domiciliation agent confirming availability of the registered office address to serve as the statutory seat of the SCSp from the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request or name search printout
Signed registered office address consent (landlord or domiciliation agent)
Copy of the lease agreement or domiciliation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the address is rejected, provide a secondary name and an alternative registered office address, or file an appeal against the decision of the LBR within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Partnership Agreement and Capital Subscription Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended for authentication) and all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement in accordance with the SCSp provisions of the Luxembourg Companies Act. The agreement must identify the sole general partner and the limited partners, define the profit-sharing ratio, and set out the capital subscription schedule. If notarization is not chosen, execute the agreement under private signatures with apostilles or certified translations where foreign partners are involved.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card copies of all partners and the general partner
Proof of residential address of each partner
Draft partnership agreement and capital subscription schedule
Certificate of good standing or equivalent corporate documents for legal entity partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies inconsistencies in the agreement, execute a rectification deed or an addendum to the partnership agreement before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Formation Dossier with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic formation dossier via the LBR portal. Attach the signed partnership agreement, written acceptance of office by the manager, the registered office consent, and proof of identity for all signatories. Participate in the anti-money-laundering/KYC verification process as requested by the RCS.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (private deed or notarial act)
Declaration of acceptance of office by the manager (gérant)
Registered office consent and lease excerpt
Identity documents of partners and manager
Unknown/negative background check certificates for the general partner and manager (e.g., Luxembourg criminal record or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification request, respond through the LBR portal within 3 months and submit a corrective deed or additional documentation. Failure to respond results in rejection; the applicant can refile after correcting the errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et des sociétés en commandite (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Official Electronic Collection of Companies (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, prepare the legal excerpt to be published in the RES. The domiciliation agent or the designated attorney must submit the publication text via the LBR interoperability module. Once published, an official publication proof (extract) is obtained for subsequent banking and commercial formalities.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (negotiated copy issued after step 3)
Text of the legal announcement derived from the partnership agreement
Power of attorney authorizing the attorney or domiciliation agent to submit the RES publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains errors, apply for a corrective notice to the RES through LBR and pay the corresponding amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Security and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Tax Administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS registration certificate to register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT and to enroll any employees with the CCSS. For electronically supplied goods, complete the intra-EU distance selling registration if required. Apply to the Luxembourg direct tax administration for a business identification number and confirm the pass-through tax classification of the SCSp.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RES publication proof
Partnership agreement and manager appointment act
Bank account opening confirmation or declaration from Luxembourg credit institution
Passport copies and proof of foreign VAT registrations for non-resident partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT or CCSS rejects the registration due to incomplete KYC, supplement the file with additional corporate documents or personal proof of the managers, and resubmit via the respective online channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, SMEs and Economic Promotion (Autorisation d'établissement division)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Establishment Authorization for Distance Retailing of Electro-technical Equipment and Energy Storage Devices (under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to crafts, commercial activities, trade and professional activities)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration-only under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 July 1998 (as amended); no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required for warehouse operations storing less than 50 tonnes of batteries and photovoltaic panels.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the EU Directive 2006/66/EC on batteries and accumulators; registration of the operator in the national WEEE register for electrical and electronic equipment; VOC emissions from storage areas must remain below the thresholds of the Industrial Emissions Directive; wastewater discharges are prohibited in the retail distribution activity, and any washing activities must be connected to a municipal sewers permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CGDIS (Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours) fire safety certificate for battery storage areas, including automatic fire detection and fire-extinguishing systems; ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) workplace safety and health clearance; structural load inspection of the logistics warehouse by an approved engineering office to ensure safe handling of lithium-ion battery stacks; obligation to maintain emergency evacuation plans and fire load documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes / ACD) — https://impotsdirects.public.lu; Registration, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA / AEDT) for VAT and registration duties — https://pfi.public.lu; unified digital procedure portal: MyGuichet.lu — https://guichet.public.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned SCSp entering the Luxembourg tax net: (1) execute a notarial deed constituting the SCSp and publish a notice in the RESA electronic official gazette; (2) register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), obtaining the 13-digit national registration number (matricule) for the SCSp and its general partner; (3) file the standard VAT registration form with the AEDT (or through MyGuichet.lu). The SCSp, although devoid of legal personality, is a distinct taxable person for VAT under Article 2 of the Law of 12 February 1979 and receives its own LU-prefixed 8-digit VAT identification number; (4) optionally register for the Union One-Stop Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) for intra-EU and import distance-sale e-commerce; (5) for direct taxes, maintain the default fiscally transparent status with the ACD, or file the Article 14(4) corporate-tax election if the SCSp is to be treated as a société de capitaux.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default; partners report their distributive share directly. Under Article 14(4) of the Law of 23 July 2016, an irrevocable election may be filed with the ACD to subject the SCSp to entity-level corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax where all general and limited partners are corporations or comparable entities subject to corporate income tax. No IRS-style check-the-box regime exists. Cross-border hybrid mismatch situations may override transparency under the Luxembourg transposition of ATAD (Articles 168ter/168quater LIR), requiring the taxpayer to document and self-assess its entity-level tax treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA), implemented by the Law of 12 February 1979 and aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the Luxembourg small-business exemption (franchise en base) under Article 57 of the VAT Law, effective 1 January 2025 (previously EUR 30,000). Non-established foreign sellers have no local exemption threshold: any taxable supply in Luxembourg requires VAT registration unless covered by the Union OSS or IOSS regime. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold for all taxable persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based transmission, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) system applies to standard B2B/B2C transactions. PEPPOL-compliant electronic invoicing is mandatory only for B2G/public procurement contracts (since 1 March 2021). All invoices must satisfy Article 3h of the VAT Law regarding authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility; SAF-T is not mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of portable power generators, solar photovoltaic panels, and accessories qualify for zero-rating under Article 45 of the Luxembourg VAT Law where (i) the goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier or for the supplier's account to a destination outside the European Union; (ii) the goods physically leave EU customs territory; and (iii) the supplier possesses, before the filing deadline of the VAT return covering the transaction, conclusive documentary evidence of exit, retained for audit. Non-EU B2B services and related intangible services are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply and reverse-charge rules; OSS/IOSS cannot be used for sales of goods exported outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic ECS export declaration with validated Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading (or CMR/Air Waybill for land/air transport) evidencing dispatch to a non-EU consignee and the customs office of exit
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT confirmation or credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the contractual currency)

Commercial invoice in EU format including HS tariff classification for solar photovoltaic modules (HS 8541.43) and portable battery generators (HS 8507.60/8507.80 as applicable), Incoterms, price, and currency
Packing list and proof of physical exit (customs release notification / ICS-ECS exit reference)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the Customs and Excise Administration may audit export zero-rating claims and require production of the full export file. Absent valid export proof, VAT is clawed back retrospectively at the standard 17% rate together with monthly late interest of 0.8% under Article 89 of the VAT Law. Civil fines under Articles 86-87 of the VAT Law range from EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 and may equal the amount of tax evaded; deliberate fraud triggers criminal sanctions including imprisonment of up to five years and fines under the General Tax Law and the Criminal Code. Payment service provider data under the CESOP regime are cross-checked against OSS/IOSS returns and export declarations, generating audit flags for non-repatriated export proceeds (Luxembourg fiscal law imposes no statutory FX repatriation period; the 180-day benchmark is retained as the standard trade-finance and credit-covenant convention).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the national central bank and euro-area monetary authority; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the prudential banking, payment-institution and AML/CFT enforcement authority; monetary policy and foreign-reserve management are exercised by the European Central Bank (ECB). Luxembourg has no separate national foreign-exchange administration because the euro is fully convertible and all capital movements are liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; any change in partnership interests must be filed with RBE within one month of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation by 31 March is an administrative offence; fines may reach EUR 125,000 with imprisonment up to three years for intentional non-compliance; repeated default exposes the entity to RBE enforcement proceedings and ultimate judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and publication with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end; extension available only if approved by the partnership agreement or the general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the seven-month period exposes the gérant to fines of up to EUR 10,000; after formal notice, the RCS may recommend compulsory judicial dissolution for persistent default, equivalent to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual transparent partnership income declaration (fiscally transparent SCSp tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March following the tax year; a qualified Luxembourg tax advisor may obtain an administrative extension normally expiring on 31 December of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 0.6% per month, capped at 10%, plus late-payment interest; failure to file permits ex officio assessment, administrative fines, and denial of certain evidentiary benefits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory where the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce of 50 employees. Entities below these thresholds qualify for audit exemption unless the partnership agreement or a partner validly requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 15 February 2018 on annual accounts and consolidated accounts, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any transfer, acquisition, or substitution of partnership interests must be recorded in the on-site register of partners and reported to the RBE within one month. Thereafter, an annual RBE confirmation of all current beneficial owners must be filed by 31 March of each calendar year. The gérant must certify that no shareholding movement has been omitted; failing to record a transfer constitutes an administrative offence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Membres) showing all partnership-interest transfers and current allocations
Register of Directors and Gérants (Managers) with powers and resignation records
Minute Book containing partner resolutions, written consents, and management decisions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City headline rate for a taxable corporate (17% national CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax + 7% unemployment/solidarity surcharge; effective 18.19% national component). The SCSp is fiscally transparent: no CIT, municipal business tax or net wealth tax at entity level; partners are taxed on allocated profits at their own rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential deduction schemes apply to the SCSp itself. Available reliefs: participation exemption (0% on qualifying dividend and capital gains), 80% exemption on net IP income, reduced 15% CIT rate on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profits for small entities, and loss flow-through at partner level for transparent partnerships.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiration under Luxembourg LIR Art. 114; carryforward restricted where a change in business/activity occurs or under anti-abuse continuity rules; losses flow through to partners of a transparent SCSp)
